choices.A: If there are more objects than drawers, at least one drawer must contain at least 2 objects.
choices.B: Each drawer can contain only 1 object.
choices.C: The number of objects must equal the number of drawers.

question: What does the pigeonhole principle state?
solution: With more objects than drawers, putting at most one object in each drawer cannot fit all the objects. At least one drawer must therefore contain at least 2 objects. This is the simplest case of the pigeonhole principle. The answer is A.
